name: Project-MONAI/MONAI
what_it_is: MONAI (Medical Open Network for AI) is a PyTorch-based open-source framework for deep learning in healthcare imaging. It provides domain-specific components for building, training, and evaluating medical image analysis models, including segmentation, classification, and detection tasks.
components: engines (training and evaluation loop runners, pytorch-ignite based)
inferers (inference strategies including sliding window, patch-based)
bundle (MONAI Bundle format for portable model configs)
configuration: Multi-GPU / multi-node data parallelism (via PyTorch DistributedDataParallel)
Optional dependencies (nibabel, ITK, cucim, openslide, mlflow, clearml, etc.)
Docker base image (PYTORCH_IMAGE build arg, default nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch)
Shared memory size (--shm-size for slim image)
modes: Auto3DSeg mode (automated 3D segmentation with NAS-style selection)
constraints: GPU (NVIDIA CUDA) required for full performance; cucim GPU acceleration only available on Linux
No built-in DICOM networking or PACS connectivity; imaging I/O depends on third-party libs (nibabel, ITK, openslide)
MONAI Bundle format requires JSON/YAML schema compliance; not interoperable with other model-serving formats out of the box
Transformers integration capped at <4.41.0 for Python <= 3.10
notable_absences: No DICOM server or PACS integration
No built-in model serving / REST inference endpoint
No built-in dataset registry or data versioning
